newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says not mulling market operations ban on DKB.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says not mulling market operations ban on DKB.

text.p: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) has not yet considered suspending Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) from the central bank's market operations, a senior BOJ official said on Tuesday.
Asked if the central bank is considering suspending DKB from market operations, the official said, "At this point, there is no truth to such speculation."
"The BOJ is keeping an eye on prosecutors' investigation of the bank," he added.
The financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Tuesday that the BOJ is considering punitive measures against DKB and suspending the bank from taking part in BOJ market operations.
The BOJ conducts market operations with major domestic and foreign dealers in each financial market the central bank uses, another BOJ official said.
The BOJ's current operations include sales and purchases of bills and Treasury bills as well as outright buying of Japanese government bonds.

Domestic media said on Tuesday that prosecutors were questioning Ichiro Fujita, a DKB vice president who had been slated to become president later this month, as well as other former and current DKB executives, in connection with a racketeer payoff scandal which has already ensnared Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
The scandal has so far led to the arrests of 10 people, including four DKB officials and a former Nomura president.

The prosecutors' latest moves, which domestic media said reflected a growing suspicion that top DKB management was involved in the scandal, came as the bank announced a new executive line-up on Tuesday which it said was untainted by the affair.
